solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Will reviewing exploration take a short time?

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so the first word grips the following pieces inside itself

parts.note: a probe is an exploratory investigation
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether looking into a will is a quick job.
explanation.walkthrough: PROBE holds A and T: PROB(A T)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the legal process in which a court examines and proves a dead person's testament as valid.

clue.text: Intimate union is source of funding

parts.note: intimate in the sense of personal, not public
Equity is the British trade union for actors and performers

explanation.surface: A close relationship described as the place money comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate union' reads like a marriage; in fact it is two pieces, a synonym and the name of a particular trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Private equity is capital invested in companies not listed on the stock exchange, a common way businesses are financed.

clue.text: One ignores problem in beheading wealthiest

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, so the opening letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: wealthiest means most rich

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a difficulty by cutting down the richest people.
explanation.walkthrough: Wealthiest becomes the two words MOST RICH; losing the M leaves OSTRICH.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is popularly said to bury its head in the sand, so a person avoiding unpleasant facts is called one.

clue.text: Path to hollow victory snatched away

indicators.note: something snatched away is taken out, so that letter is removed from the word for hollow

parts.note: a hollow is a valley or low-lying dip
V for victory, the familiar abbreviation

explanation.surface: A route leading to a win that turns out empty after being taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow victory' looks like a single phrase, but hollow is a noun for the dip in the ground and victory is just V.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow passage or lane, a kind of walkway between buildings.

clue.text: Charles I was accomplished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put to death, as the English king was beheaded in 1649
second meaning: carried out or performed

explanation.surface: A historical remark that King Charles I was a skilled man.
explanation.walkthrough: Accomplished seems to praise the king's talents, but here it is a past participle meaning carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both put to death by sentence and carried out to completion, as a plan or task is.

clue.text: Look for good weapon

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lance is a long spear carried by a horseman

explanation.surface: Searching for a decent weapon to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a brief look, so the noun and verb senses match a quick peek.

clue.text: Manages to exchange drug for a literary character

indicators.note: to exchange one thing for another is to swap it out, so one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: gets by means manages or copes
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody contrives to swap narcotics for something.
explanation.walkthrough: In GETS BY the E is swapped for A. The 'a' does double duty in the surface but the definition is simply a literary character.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the title figure of F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby.

clue.text: Wanted edges rubbed off with springs and chamois, perhaps

indicators.note: with the edges worn away only the inner part of the word survives

parts.note: the word without its outside letters
lopes as a verb: bounds along with long strides

explanation.surface: A worn-out item restored using springs and a polishing cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamois looks like the soft cleaning leather, which fits 'rubbed', but here it is the animal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a goat-antelope of European mountains, so it is one example of these hoofed grazing animals.

clue.text: Company car driven up to the French boat

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A firm's vehicle being driven to a French destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker covered with hide, traditional in Wales.

clue.text: Reason client let out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, put out of their places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer explains why a customer was released.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason as a noun means the power of thinking and understanding, the mind's rational faculty.

clue.text: Drone goes through Martian surface

parts.note: the informal American spelling

indicators.note: the surface of something is its outermost layer, here taken as the word's opening letter

parts.note: just the start of the word

explanation.surface: An unmanned craft passes through the face of Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: Drone suggests a flying machine and 'Martian surface' a planetary landscape; drone is actually a low hum.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low humming sound, the same as a monotonous buzz or hum.

clue.text: Decoration makes armed forces furious

parts.note: the military are the armed forces
cross means angry

explanation.surface: An award for bravery leaves the services enraged.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Cross is a British gallantry medal for army officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal awarded for bravery is a decoration, an honour pinned on a uniform.

clue.text: "Good will to all men," is taught yearly for starting letters

indicators.note: the clue says outright that only the opening letters of the following words are used

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A Christmas message of peace and goodwill is taught every year.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation from the Christmas story seems to be the whole definition, but only its first two words define; the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity means friendship and peaceful relations, a spirit of kindly feeling between people.

clue.text: After editing album clip, I remove power cord

indicators.note: editing material rearranges it, so these letters are reworked
to remove something is to take it out of the collected letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A music editor cuts the power lead after trimming a track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power cord' looks like an electrical lead; power is just P to be taken away from the letters of album clip I.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbilical is short for umbilical cord, which connects a foetus to the placenta.

clue.text: Ten plus three worked out by network of computers

indicators.note: something worked out has been processed and reshaped, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum of thirteen calculated by a computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is arithmetic, but the numbers are spelt-out words supplying letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired technology linking computers in a local area network.

clue.text: Political dissident fires nuke in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns everything over, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel launches a nuclear weapon during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusenik originally named Soviet Jews refused exit visas, later any protester who refuses to comply with authority.

clue.text: Most suitable journalists are on trial

parts.note: AP is the Associated Press news agency
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: The best-placed reporters are being tried in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On trial' suggests a courtroom, but trial only means an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting or appropriate, and this is its superlative form meaning the most fitting.

clue.text: Indicator of veins on pitch

parts.note: lodes are veins of metal ore in rock
pitch is a black tarry substance

explanation.surface: A miner's sign that seams of ore lie under the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the first piece above the second in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used to steer by, especially the Pole Star, so a guide pointing the way.

clue.text: Question a very loud opening in storm drains

parts.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question
taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: just the start of the word

explanation.surface: Asking why there is a thunderous gap in the storm sewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm drains' reads as one thing; drains is a verb meaning drinks up.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaff is to drink heartily, and drains means downs a drink to the last drop.

clue.text: Lead a high card, then tense up inside

indicators.note: inside tells us this piece goes within the earlier one

parts.note: the ace is the highest card in many games

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tense in the sense of tight or stretched

explanation.surface: A card player opens with a top card, then gets nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the card-play term to open a trick, but it is the definition, as a verb meaning drive or set going.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate is to cause something to operate or to motivate someone, similar to driving or prompting them.

clue.text: Cobweb sags more after being ripped apart

indicators.note: something ripped apart is in pieces that can be put back together in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spider's web droops further once it has been torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is the fine filmy silk spun by small spiders, seen on grass or floating in air.

clue.text: Approval for staff meeting

parts.note: to man is to staff, as in manning a desk
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Permission granted for an office get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official authority or endorsement, such as voters grant to a government.

clue.text: Sharpness of woman's buckle

parts.note: wit means mental sharpness or cleverness
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: How sharp the clasp on a lady's belt is.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckle looks like a fastening but is a verb: to give way or collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and droop, collapsing in the way something buckles under pressure.

clue.text: Organ is faintest in echoing section

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a whole, so the letters run inside the words shown

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: A church organ sounds quietest in a part of the building with an echo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echoing' tempts a solver to read letters backwards, but it is just part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestine is the long tube of the gut, an internal body organ that digests food.

clue.text: He refuses to believe top general could hold up American city

indicators.note: turned up, the letters face the other way
holding something means having it inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: CIC stands for commander-in-chief
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A doubter thinks a senior commander might delay an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning delay; it splits into a containment and a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic distrusts people's sincerity and doubts motives, so he is someone inclined to disbelief.

clue.text: Falsifies accounts, but caught replacing first entry

indicators.note: this says the opening letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: a firm's accounts are its books
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fraudster doctors the accounts but is caught out by the first item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsifies accounts' reads as one phrase, an echo of 'cooks the books'; only the verb defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook figures is an idiom for altering records dishonestly, which is to fake or doctor them.

clue.text: Long period of time before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long period' looks like one phrase; long is a verb meaning to pine.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to desire it intensely, the same as pining or hankering.

clue.text: Spicy vegetable and pickle

parts.note: hot food is spicy
a potato is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A chilli-laced vegetable served with chutney.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickle looks like the preserved condiment; it means a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an awkward controversial issue, and a pickle is an informal word for a difficult predicament.

clue.text: Turkey might be kept up in good spirits

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a bird, standing for the noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bird that pecks at its food

definitions.note: a phrase describing the thing kept up, standing for the noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the British phrase 'keep your ___ up' means stay cheerful

explanation.surface: A turkey managing to stay cheerful, perhaps before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your pecker up' is a British idiom urging someone to stay cheerful; pecker there means courage or spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Any bird that pecks can be called one, and in the British phrase the word stands for one's spirit or pluck.

clue.text: Religious Jamaicans uttered lines on television

indicators.note: uttered means spoken out loud, so we go by how the word sounds

parts.note: Rastas are Rastafarians, members of a Jamaican religious movement; in a non-rhotic accent the two sound alike

explanation.surface: Devout Jamaicans speaking their lines on a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines on television' suggests an actor's script; it means the scan lines that make up the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A raster is the pattern of horizontal scanning rows that build up the image on a cathode-ray screen.
